How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows you how to **generate a RESTful API request** for the *“get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll walk you through the UI steps, then give you a ready‑to‑copy cURL command and a short Python snippet that uses the `requests_get` helper you mentioned. --- ## 1. Find the Endpoint in the Dashboard | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **Open the Dashboard** | Log into your Cisco Nexus Dashboard instance (e.g., `https:///`). | You need to be authenticated to see the API Explorer. | | **Navigate to “API Explorer”** | In the left‑hand menu, click **Developer → API Explorer**. | This is where all documented APIs live. | | **Locate the API** | Search for “device connector versions” or look under the **Device Management** section. | The API you’re after is usually grouped by functional area. | | **Select the API** | Click the entry titled **Get Information of Device Connector Versions**. | This opens the detailed view. | > **Tip:** If you can’t find it, use the search bar at the top of the API Explorer and type “connector versions”. --- ## 2. Inspect the API Details Once you’ve selected the API, you’ll see: | Section | What you’ll see | How to use it | |---------|-----------------|---------------| | **Endpoint URL** | `/api/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions` | This is the path you’ll hit. | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | The verb you’ll use. | | **Query Parameters** | e.g., `?deviceId=12345&status=active` | Optional filters; fill them if needed. | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | Required for auth & content negotiation. | | **Sample Response** | A JSON blob showing the structure of the returned data. | Helps you understand what fields you’ll receive. | --- ## 3. Generate the Request | Step | What to do | Why | |------|------------|-----| | **Fill in Parameters** | If the API requires a device ID or other filters, enter them in the “Parameters” pane. | Makes the request specific to your needs. | | **Click “Generate Request”** | At the bottom of the page, press the **Generate Request** button. | The Dashboard will build a ready‑to‑copy cURL command. | | **Copy the cURL** | Copy the generated command from the “Generated cURL” box. | You can paste it into a terminal or Postman. | > **Example Generated cURL** > ```bash > curl -X GET "https:///api/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345" \ > -H "accept: application/json" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " > ``` --- ## 4. Test the Request ### Using cURL ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` ### Using Postman 1. Create a new **GET** request. 2. Paste the full URL (`https:///api/v6.3.1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345`). 3. Under **Headers**, add: * `accept: application/json` * `Authorization: Bearer ` 4. Hit **Send**. You should receive a JSON payload similar to the sample shown in the API Explorer. --- ## 5. Call the API from Python (using the helper) If you prefer to embed the call in a script, here’s a minimal example using the `requests_get` helper you supplied: ```python from functions import requests_get # Replace with your actual values BASE_URL = "https:///api/v6.3.1" ENDPOINT = "/device-connector-versions" DEVICE_ID = "12345" # Build the full URL url = f"{BASE_URL}{ENDPOINT}" # Optional query parameters params = {"deviceId": DEVICE_ID} # Make the GET request response = requests_get(url=url, params=params) # Print the JSON response print(response) ``` > **Important:** > * The helper assumes you’ve already handled authentication (e.g., by setting a global `requests.Session` with the bearer token). > * If you haven’t, you can pass the `headers` argument explicitly: > ```python > headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer ", "Accept": "application/json"} > response = requests_get(url=url, params=params, headers=headers) > ``` --- ## 6. Common Pitfalls & Quick Fixes | Issue | Symptom | Fix | |-------|---------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Server returns 401. | Verify the access token is still valid and has the required scopes. | | **404 Not Found** | Endpoint not found. | Double‑check the base URL and API version (`/api/v6.3.1/...`). | | **400 Bad Request** | Missing required parameter. | Ensure you’ve supplied all mandatory query parameters (e.g., `deviceId`). | | **Rate‑limit Exceeded** | 429 Too Many Requests. | Add retry logic or throttle your calls. | --- ## 7. Summary Checklist - [ ] Logged into Cisco Nexus Dashboard. - [ ] Located the **Get Information of Device Connector Versions** API. - [ ] Generated the cURL command. - [ ] Tested the request via cURL/Postman. - [ ] (Optional) Implemented the call in Python using `requests_get`. That’s it! You now know exactly how to generate, test, and consume the *Device Connector Versions* API in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy coding!
